title: Resolve the imports
description:
At load time, every import must be found or the program does not start. Write the check the loader makes:

```cpp
std::string resolveImports(const std::map<std::string, std::set<std::string>>& exportsByDll,
                           const std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::string>>& imports);
```

- `exportsByDll` maps each DLL that **exists** to the names it exports.
- `imports` is the program's import table: pairs of (DLL name, function name), in order.
- DLL names ignore upper and lower case (`KERNEL32.dll` is `kernel32.dll`); function names do not.

Return the message for the **first** import that fails, or an empty string if all of them resolve:

- DLL not found: `The code execution cannot proceed because <dll> was not found.`
- Function not exported: `The procedure entry point <function> could not be located in the dynamic link library <dll>.`

Use the DLL name as the import table spells it.
hints: Build a lookup from lower-case DLL name to that DLL's export set first, then walk the imports in order.
